criteria.description: Basic principles (TRL 1): the report states the scientific or engineering principles on which the assessed technology is based, citing observations, studies or literature.
Concept formulated (TRL 2): the report describes a practical application of those principles and how the assessed technology is intended to work in it.
Proof of concept (TRL 3): the report presents analytical or laboratory results that demonstrate the critical function or characteristic of the assessed technology.
Laboratory validation (TRL 4): the report states that the assessed component or a low-fidelity breadboard was tested in a laboratory environment and reports the results.

Relevant-environment validation (TRL 5): the report states that the assessed component or breadboard was tested in a simulated or relevant environment representative of the intended environment, and reports the results.
Prototype in relevant environment (TRL 6): the report states that a representative model or prototype of the assessed system or subsystem was demonstrated in a relevant environment.
Prototype in operational environment (TRL 7): the report states that a prototype close to the final configuration was demonstrated in the actual operational environment.
System qualified (TRL 8): the report states that the final system was completed and qualified through test and demonstration against its requirements.
Proven in operation (TRL 9): the report states that the final system was used successfully in actual operations or deployment over a stated period.
Quantified results against requirements: the report compares measured performance with stated requirements or acceptance criteria and says whether they were met.

Environment and test article defined: the report describes the test conditions and the configuration or fidelity of the tested article (for example breadboard, prototype, production unit) relative to the intended application.

Evidence matches the assessment target: the cited evidence concerns the assessed target itself (component, subsystem, system or technology), not a different element or only the parent project as a whole.
